import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Set up the figure with multiple subplots for comprehensive visualization
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle('Titanic Passenger Survival Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=1.02)

# Plot 1: Survival rate by passenger class and sex
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
survival_by_class_sex = df.groupby(['pclass', 'sex'])['survived'].mean().unstack()
survival_by_class_sex.plot(kind='bar', ax=ax1, color=['#ff6b6b', '#4ecdc4'], edgecolor='black')
ax1.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=11)
ax1.set_title('Survival Rate by Class and Sex', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xticklabels(['1st Class', '2nd Class', '3rd Class'], rotation=0)
ax1.legend(title='Sex', loc='upper right')
ax1.set_ylim(0, 1)
for container in ax1.containers:
    ax1.bar_label(container, fmt='%.2f', fontsize=9)

# Plot 2: Age distribution by survival status
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
colors = {'Survived': '#4ecdc4', 'Did Not Survive': '#ff6b6b'}
df_age = df.dropna(subset=['age'])
sns.kdeplot(data=df_age[df_age['survived']==1], x='age', ax=ax2, 
            label='Survived', color='#4ecdc4', fill=True, alpha=0.5)
sns.kdeplot(data=df_age[df_age['survived']==0], x='age', ax=ax2, 
            label='Did Not Survive', color='#ff6b6b', fill=True, alpha=0.5)
ax2.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=11)
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.legend(loc='upper right')

# Plot 3: Fare distribution by class (box plot)
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
palette = {1: '#2ecc71', 2: '#3498db', 3: '#e74c3c'}
sns.boxplot(data=df, x='pclass', y='fare', hue='survived', ax=ax3, 
            palette=['#ff6b6b', '#4ecdc4'])
ax3.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_ylabel('Fare (£)', fontsize=11)
ax3.set_title('Fare Distribution by Class and Survival', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xticklabels(['1st Class', '2nd Class', '3rd Class'])
ax3.legend(title='Survived', labels=['No', 'Yes'], loc='upper right')
ax3.set_ylim(0, 300)  # Limit y-axis for better visualization

# Plot 4: Survival count by embarkation port
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
embark_survival = df.groupby(['embark_town', 'survived']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
embark_survival = embark_survival.reindex(['Southampton', 'Cherbourg', 'Queenstown'])
embark_survival.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, ax=ax4, 
                     color=['#ff6b6b', '#4ecdc4'], edgecolor='black')
ax4.set_xlabel('Embarkation Port', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Passengers', fontsize=11)
ax4.set_title('Passenger Count by Embarkation Port and Survival', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_xticklabels(ax4.get_xticklabels(), rotation=0)
ax4.legend(title='Survived', labels=['No', 'Yes'], loc='upper right')

# Add survival rates as text annotations
for i, port in enumerate(['Southampton', 'Cherbourg', 'Queenstown']):
    port_data = df[df['embark_town'] == port]
    if len(port_data) > 0:
        rate = port_data['survived'].mean()
        total = len(port_data)
        ax4.annotate(f'{rate:.1%}', xy=(i, total + 10), ha='center', fontsize=9, fontweight='bold')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
